(i) the profitability of decentralized generation technologies is highly dependent on the willingness to pay of the population, and (ii) the profitability of diesel generators is higher than that of photovoltaic systems.

the PV‐diesel option is the only one of the four options which is economically viable for the rural communities studied, and that the choice of the PV‐diesele option should be made with the highest possible PV share, which is 50 per cent in the case of the communities studied.

the profitability of the technologies is highly dependent on demand and that the profitability of solar home systems is higher than that of the other technologies, but that this is not the case for the diesel mini‐grid.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electrification of rural communities with a population of less than 200 inhabitants is not viable.

the pv‐diesel generator is the most profitable technology in all cases, the hybrid generator the least profitable; diesel mini‐grides are profitable only in the high‐income segment, and the solar home systems are profitable only for low‐income households with a low demand.

the most profitable technology depends on the level of service required and the socio‐economic conditions of the village.Originality/value – This study shows the importance of the choice of technology in the planning of rural electrification and the importance of considering the social and environmental impacts.
